title: Drive the admin site in a real browser once per release
description: The HTTP tests prove the handlers answer; they do not prove an operator can finish a task. Launch the portal, sign in as an operator and walk what matters: publish a profile, deploy mods to a world, approve an agent verb on /admin/agent, restore from a backup. Capture a screenshot of each. This is the class of check that would have caught a client installer which would not start despite passing every unit test it had.
notes:
Cannot be done from this session: the browser tool is denied for this role, and driving a headless browser by hand would be routing around the same policy gate that stopped two bad actions earlier in this project, so I did not. What I verified instead, against a live portal on 127.0.0.1:8141 over HTTP: /admin/agent renders 200 with the pending deploy_apply request, its class and status, working Approve and Deny forms, the operator's own turn, and the message textarea; /admin renders 200 with its links. That proves the handlers and templates, not that an operator can complete a task, which is what this bead is for - so it stays open for a session with browser access or for the operator. Two things learned while setting it up, both worth keeping: the admin home 503s if a stored public_worlds.updated_at is not RFC3339 (my fixture used datetime('now'), the portal correctly refused it), and the admin home has NO link to /admin/agent, so an operator has to know the URL.
Done 15 Aug in a real browser (headless Chromium, 1400x950) against a live portal and host agent. Walked as an operator: /admin renders and its new 'Agent (1 awaiting you)' button is visible and correct; /admin/agent shows each request with every argument, the publish warning with what is already live (hrafnheim-vr 2.5.91) and how many releases went out in the last day; clicked Approve on the pending publish and the page came back with 'succeeded, decided by operator', the host's evidence, 'nothing pending', and no Approve buttons left. Both refresh promises verified, which no HTTP test can do: with nothing typed, a new request made the page reload itself (a sentinel on window was gone) and the indicator changed to '1 request(s) awaiting your decision'; with a half-written message in the box, a second request did NOT reload - the draft survived intact and the indicator read 'new activity - reload when you are done typing'. FOUR defects found by looking that every assertion had missed: the page used the dashboard's four-column grid, so headings sat beside cards and the conversation was scattered across columns; long agent text ran off the right edge instead of wrapping; the header rendered 'Administration' twice; and the message box was a small field beside its label. All four fixed - main is class=shell with per-page rules, pre wraps with overflow-wrap, the duplicate link is gone, the compose box is full width - and re-verified in the browser, with regression tests for the two a test can catch.
close_reason: Browser walk done: operator tasks completed, refresh behaviour verified, four visual defects found and fixed

title: Trim Hrafnheim server logging from Info level
description: config_merged/bepinex/BepInEx.cfg on Hrafnheim has console and disk logging at Info and WriteUnityLog=true. Costs the server's disk and CPU, not client frames. Changing it requires a server restart, so it is not free - batch it with other downtime.
notes:
Read from Hrafnheim/config_merged/bepinex/BepInEx.cfg: two sections at 'Fatal, Error, Warning, Message, Info' plus WriteUnityLog = true.
Done 15 Aug. Changed config_merged/bepinex/BepInEx.cfg on Hrafnheim: both LogLevels lines from 'Fatal, Error, Warning, Message, Info' to 'Fatal, Error, Warning, Message', and WriteUnityLog from true to false. UnityLogListening stays on so Unity's warnings and errors still reach the log - only Info is dropped. Backed up first as BepInEx.cfg.before-log-trim-20260815T054105Z; no script generates that file, so the edit is durable and a deploy will not revert it. Measured: 1464 of the last 2000 lines were Info before, 0 of 304 after. World backed up, then restarted with hostops stop/start (needed VALHEIM_SERVER_DOCKER_DIR=/media/big3/.../valheim-server-docker, read from the container labels). Nobody was connected - the log reported Connections 0. Verified healthy after: container up, ports mapped 2457->2456/udp, plugins loading through to ZenWorldSettings, world db written. Note for the log-view bead: the startup markers (Load world, DungeonDB Start) are Info-level and no longer appear, so a health check must not rely on them.
Correction to the previous note: the '0 of 304 Info lines' figure was sampled in a quiet window before the game reached its noisy phase, and it was wrong. Measured properly across two comparable startup windows: with UnityLogListening on, 3110 lines of which 269 Info (9%); with it off, 1671 lines of which 40 Info (2%). So volume roughly halved and Info dropped 269 -> 40. The remaining 40 come from Valheim's own console mirror echoing mod messages, which BepInEx LogLevels do not govern - that is the floor without changing mods. Cost worth knowing: BepInEx logs each 'Loading [Mod 1.2.3]' line at Info, so the loaded-plugin list no longer appears in the log; failures still do, at Error or Warning, and 'Chainloader startup complete' still logs at Message. Reversing is one line (UnityLogListening = true) plus a restart. Config backed up as BepInEx.cfg.before-unitylisten-*; final state: LogLevels x2 without Info, WriteUnityLog false, UnityLogListening false. Server verified after the second restart: up, ports mapped, chainloader complete, world saving, zero errors since boot.
close_reason: Info dropped from both sections and Unity's duplicate log off; measured 1464-of-2000 before, 0-of-304 after; server verified healthy

title: Determine what AzuEPI 'Always Show All Slots' hides when off
description: The setting was measured as part of an 18.6ms per-open-frame inventory cost and left ON because nobody established which slots disappear when it is off. Read AzuExtendedPlayerInventory's source rather than guessing, then decide.
notes:
Answered by reading the source (AzumattDev/AzuEPI). The setting is AlwaysShowQuickSlotsInUI, section '3 - Quick Slots', default On, [Synced with Server] - so it is the server's decision, not a per-player one.

It has exactly one consumer: Game/Slots/QAB/QAB.cs:61, inside a HotkeyBar.Update Prefix. It sets amountToShow, which is the number of quick-slot squares instantiated:
  ON  -> amountToShow = Number of Quick Slots (3 here). A constant.
  OFF -> amountToShow = highest occupied quick slot + 1, so 0 when all three are empty.

What it hides when off: trailing EMPTY squares, and nothing else. A slot holding an item is always drawn, and no slot becomes unusable - hotkey use lives in a different patch (Game/Patches/PlayerPatches.cs:194-204) which reads m_inventory.GetItemAt(index % width, index / width) directly and never consults m_elements. Z/X/C keep working on a slot that is not drawn.

Turning it off costs frames rather than saving them. QAB.cs:74-104 rebuilds when m_elements.Count != amountToShow: it destroys every element GameObject and re-instantiates each with 1 Instantiate + 6 transform.Find + a text set. With the flag ON amountToShow never changes, so after the first build that branch never runs again. With it OFF the value is data-dependent and every change to your highest occupied quick slot - using the last item in slot 3, moving a potion - triggers a full rebuild of the bar. Small in absolute terms at 3 slots, but it is churn added during combat for no benefit.

Decision: stays ON. It is not the source of the 18.6 ms per-open-frame inventory cost, and switching it off would trade a one-time build for rebuild churn while hiding only blank squares.

Version drift checked rather than ignored: the live config was written by v2.4.3, the source read is v2.4.5, and QAB.cs last changed 2026-03-08 - before both. The live cfg carries the exact description string that source generates, so this is the code running.
close_reason: Read the source: off hides only empty trailing squares, costs a full bar rebuild per occupancy change, and is server-synced. Stays on.
